ColemanPowerSeries.summary: The libraries hold only general inputs. These are cyclotomic extensions of an arbitrary field, norms of ζ−1 over a base where the cyclotomic polynomial is irreducible, Mathlib's power-series derivative, substitution and Weierstrass preparation, the Amice transform D(Z_p,Z_p) ≃ Z_p[[X]], Tau Ceti's Teichmüller lift and unit filtration for local fields, the elementary cyclotomic-unit lemmas and CM-field unit indices. Genuinely missing: the local tower Q_p(μ_{p^n}) with its degree and ramification, norm-compatible inverse limits and the Z_p[[G]]-action, Coleman's norm operator and Theorem 10.13, ψ and the Coleman map, the fundamental exact sequence, and the cyclotomic-unit quotient theorem 12.23.

targets.target: Local cyclotomic fields K_n = Q_p(mu_{p^n}) with integer rings and local-field structure
targets.note: CyclotomicField (p^n) ℚ_[p] exists because cyclotomic extensions are defined over any field, and Tau Ceti makes the completion of a Dedekind domain with finite residue field a local field, which covers ℚ(ζ_{p^n}) completed above p. Missing: identifying that completion with ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}), its ring of integers ℤ_p[ζ] (Mathlib's ℤ[ζ] result is over ℚ), and a local-field structure on arbitrary finite extensions of ℚ_[p].

targets.target: Compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity (ζ_{p^{n+1}}^p = ζ_{p^n})
targets.note: Only the single-step fact that a power of a primitive root is primitive of the quotient order; no chosen compatible system or tower of roots.

targets.target: Degree [K_n:Q_p] = φ(p^n), total ramification, uniformizer ζ_{p^n}−1 and residue field F_p
targets.note: The degree formula needs Irreducible (cyclotomic (p^n) ℚ_[p]), which is not proved (Eisenstein-ness is stated over ℤ only). Total ramification, the prime ζ−1 and inertia degree 1 are proved for ℚ(ζ_{p^n}) and, in Tau Ceti, for number fields unramified at p, not for the local field.

targets.target: Transitivity of field norms in the tower K_{n+1}/K_n/Q_p
targets.note: Norm_{A/R} = Norm_{S/R} ∘ Norm_{A/S} for any tower of commutative rings with A free over S, which covers the tower of finite field extensions.

targets.target: Norm identities N_{K_{n+1}/K_n}(ζ_{p^{n+1}}−1)=ζ_{p^n}−1 and continuity of the norm on units
targets.note: Mathlib computes the norm of ζ−1 only down to a base over which the whole cyclotomic polynomial is irreducible (value p); the relative step K_{n+1}/K_n and continuity of Algebra.norm are not stated.

targets.target: Norm-compatible units U_∞ as an inverse limit; principal units as a compact Z_p-module
targets.note: Principal units and the compactness of each U(K,i) exist at a single finite level, and ℤ_[p] is a binomial ring so (1+X)^a is defined formally for a ∈ ℤ_[p]. The inverse limit under norms and the Z_p-module structure on principal units are absent (the latter is a TODO in PowerSeries/Binomial.lean).

targets.target: Continuous action of the completed group ring Z_p[[G]] extending the Galois action
targets.note: Neither library defines completed group rings or Iwasawa algebras; Mathlib only has the Amice transform for measures on Z_p.

targets.target: Decomposition U_∞ = μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1} for odd p
targets.note: At a single level of a local field, Tau Ceti's Teichmüller lift is a multiplicative section with image μ_{q−1}, and Mathlib identifies units modulo principal units with residue units. The product splitting is not stated even at finite level, and nothing is done on the inverse limit.

targets.target: The Tate-module subgroup Z_p(1) of U_∞
targets.note: Only the p-adic cyclotomic character of a ring automorphism exists; the Tate module lim μ_{p^n} as a subgroup of norm-compatible units is absent.

targets.target: Coefficient extension and the semilocal version for an unramified coefficient extension
targets.note: No semilocal cyclotomic units or unramified coefficient extensions of the local tower in either library.

duplicates.note: That layer states 𝒪[K]ˣ ≃ μ_{q−1} × U(K,1) and the pro-p structure of principal units, the finite-level form of this layer's U_∞ = μ_{p−1} × U_{∞,1}.
Owns completed group rings and their universal property for continuous actions, which this layer re-asks for when extending the G-action to Z_p[[G]].

targets.target: O[[T]] finite free over φ(O[[T]]), φ(T)=(1+T)^p−1, with explicit basis (1+T)^i
targets.note: Substitution of power series exists; the finiteness and freeness of O[[T]] over the image of φ is not proved.

targets.target: Coleman norm operator N defined by the determinant of multiplication, and the trace
targets.note: Algebra.norm (determinant of left multiplication) and trace are general, so the definition is available once the finite-free structure is proved; the operator on O[[T]] and its properties are absent.

targets.target: Identification of N(f) with ∏_{ξ∈μ_p} f(ξ(1+T)−1) after adjoining μ_p
targets.note: Mathlib's product formula for norms is over fields with embeddings into an algebraically closed field, not for this power-series extension.

targets.target: Integrality of the normalized trace and its identification with ψ
targets.note: No ψ operator on power series in either library.

targets.target: Norm/trace compatibility with evaluation at ξ_{p^n}−1, the congruences of RJW Lemma 10.11 and continuity
targets.note: Only general evaluation of power series at topologically nilpotent elements exists.

targets.target: Uniqueness of the interpolating unit power series, via Weierstrass preparation over O[[T]]
targets.note: Weierstrass preparation is proved over any complete local ring for series with nonzero reduction, so it covers O[[T]] for a complete DVR O. Missing: the consequence that a series vanishing at all ξ_{p^n}−1 is zero, and the uniqueness of the interpolating unit.

targets.target: Coleman's theorem 10.13: U_∞ ≃ {f ∈ Z_p[[T]]^× : N(f) = f} with interpolation f(ξ_{p^n}−1)=u_n
targets.note: No Coleman power series, norm-compatible units or interpolation theorem.

duplicates.note: PG.4 constructs ψ from the finite-free φ-coordinate decomposition (normalized trace) and proves its integrality and continuity, the same construction this layer asks for on O[[T]].
L2 defines φ(T)=(1+T)^p−1 and ψ with ψφ=1 on O[[T]] ≅ measures, overlapping the ψ identification here.
L4 owns Weierstrass division and preparation for O[[T]], which Mathlib already proves over complete local rings.

targets.target: Logarithmic derivative Δ(f)=∂f/f with ∂=(1+T)d/dT on unit power series
targets.note: The formal derivative as a derivation (with inverse and chain rules) exists; the operator ∂ and the homomorphism Δ from units to O[[T]] are not defined.

targets.target: Amice transform A between measures on Z_p and Z_p[[T]] (with inverse)
targets.note: Linear equivalence D(ℤ_[p],ℤ_[p]) ≃ ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ with coefficients μ(binom(x,n)); only ℤ_[p] coefficients are bundled as an equivalence.

targets.target: Operators on measures: 1−φψ as restriction to Z_p^×, ∂ as multiplication by x, and ∂^{-1} on ψ=0 via x^{-1}
targets.note: No φ, ψ, restriction to units or multiplication-by-x operators on measures or power series.

targets.target: The Coleman map Col_0 = A^{-1}∘∂^{-1}∘(1−φψ)∘Δ∘Coleman and the computation Col_0(c(a)) = −([a]−1)ζ_p
targets.note: Depends on Coleman power series and the p-adic zeta pseudo-measure, neither of which exists.

targets.target: Sign-adjusted Col = −Col_0 with proved comparison; additivity, continuity, Z_p-linearity and G-equivariance
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: L2 builds ∂=(1+T)d/dT, φ, ψ, restriction to units as 1−φψ and inversion of multiplication by x on units, the operators in this layer's Col_0 pipeline.
Also states restriction, φ, ψ, differentiation and division by x on distributions supported on units, extending the same operators.

targets.target: Exact sequence for the logarithmic derivative on norm-invariant units (mod-p computation, lifting, compactness)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Exact sequence for 1−φ on ψ=1 via the convergent sum of φ-iterates and evaluation at T=0
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Kernel of Col_0 is μ_{p−1}×Z_p(1) and cokernel Z_p(1) via the cyclotomic moment
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Fundamental exact sequence 0→Z_p(1)→U_{∞,1}→Z_p[[G]]→Z_p(1)→0 (RJW Theorem 12.17), topological and algebraic
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Finite-flat coefficient extension O⊗_{Z_p} of the sequence with completed-tensor comparison
targets.note: Exactness of tensoring with a flat module and the comparison of adic completion with base change for finite modules over Noetherian rings are general Mathlib results; the specific sequence and its topological version are absent.

targets.target: Global cyclotomic unit group D_n (roots of unity and cyclotomic differences, intersected with units)
targets.note: Mathlib proves that (ζ^a−1)/(ζ−1) is a unit and that ζ^a−1 and ζ−1 are associated for a prime to n; the subgroup D_n and its structure are not defined.

targets.target: Real generators γ_{n,a}, retaining −1 at finite level, and the identities of RJW §12.3
targets.note: Mathlib has the CM structure of ℚ(ζ_n) and the index (1 or 2) of real units times roots of unity in all units; the explicit real cyclotomic generators and §12.3 identities are absent.

targets.target: Z_p-span of a finitely generated subgroup of principal units equals its closure
targets.note: No Z_p-module structure on principal units, so no such closure statement.

targets.target: Teichmüller-adjusted norm-compatible generator and inverse-limit cyclicity of cyclotomic units
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Image of the closed cyclotomic tower under Col and Theorem 12.23: U^+_{∞,1}/C^+_{∞,1} ≃ Z_p[[G^+]]/(I(G^+)ζ_p), with O-coefficients
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: L0 also defines cyclotomic units as a subgroup of actual units, relates the real and full-field groups and torsion, and gives the explicit prime-power-conductor generators this layer asks for.

DirichletPadicLFunctions.summary: Mathlib already has much of the complex side: ζ(−k) as Bernoulli numbers for every k ≥ 0, continuation and trivial zeros of Dirichlet L-functions, Euler-factor deletion under change of level, conductors and primitive characters, the Gauss-sum inversion formula, the Mellin transform, the class-number limit of ζ_K, von Staudt–Clausen, the Amice transform and the level-one E_k q-expansion. Tau Ceti adds q-expansions of f(dτ), so the p-stabilized Eisenstein series is within reach. Missing on the complex side are generalized Bernoulli numbers and L(χ,1−n), Gauss-sum nonvanishing for composite conductor, and continuation of ζ_K. All of the p-adic theory is missing: the smoothed measure, the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure and its twists, Kummer congruences, the p-adic logarithm and Leopoldt's formula, the pole at s = 1 and the Eisenstein measures.

targets.target: Mellin-transform continuation of L(f,s) for decaying f (RJW Theorem 2.4), with differentiation under the integral and values at negative integers
targets.note: Mathlib has the Mellin transform with convergence and differentiability under big-O decay bounds. The continuation of Γ(s)^{-1}·Mellin(f) to all of ℂ with L(f,−n) = (−1)^n f^{(n)}(0) is not stated.

targets.target: Application to the Bernoulli generating function t/(e^t−1) and its smoothed variant
targets.note: Only the formal power-series identity for the Bernoulli generating function exists; ζ is continued in Mathlib through Hurwitz zeta and theta functions, not through this Mellin argument, and the smoothed variant is absent.

targets.target: Special values ζ(−n) in terms of Bernoulli numbers, including the n = 0 case ζ(0) = −1/2
targets.note: Proved for every k ∈ ℕ, including k = 0 (ζ(0) = −1/2), in both Bernoulli sign conventions.

targets.target: Generalized Bernoulli numbers B_{n,χ} and L(χ,1−n) = −B_{n,χ}/n, compared with the complex L-function
targets.note: Dirichlet L-functions are continued as combinations of Hurwitz zeta functions, whose values at strictly negative integers are Bernoulli-polynomial values; the trivial zeros are proved. B_{n,χ} is not defined and the formula for L(χ,1−n) is a stated TODO in HurwitzZetaValues.lean.

targets.target: Inversion formula for Gauss sums of primitive characters
targets.note: For primitive χ mod N, g(χ, ψ_a) = χ^{-1}(a) g(χ, ψ) for every a ∈ ZMod N (including non-units), and the discrete Fourier transform of χ is χ^{-1}(−k) times the Gauss sum.

targets.target: Nonvanishing of Gauss sums of primitive Dirichlet characters
targets.note: Nonvanishing (via g(χ)g(χ^{-1}) = #R) is proved only for nontrivial characters of a finite field, i.e. prime modulus; the composite-conductor statement |g(χ)|² = N is absent.

targets.target: Conductors, primitive characters and change of level
targets.note: Characters with values in any commutative ring; primitivity of the induced primitive character is proved.

targets.target: Imprimitive Euler-factor deletion L(χ_N,s) = L(χ,s)·∏_{p|N}(1−χ(p)p^{−s})
targets.note: Stated for the continued L-functions, for all s when χ is nontrivial and for s ≠ 1 otherwise.

targets.target: Dedekind zeta: meromorphic germ at s = 1, simple pole, residue equal to the class-number limit (RJW Theorem 2.2)
targets.note: Mathlib defines ζ_K only as the Dirichlet series and proves the real one-sided limit (s−1)ζ_K(s) → residue; Tau Ceti adds the Euler product on Re s > 1. No continuation, meromorphic germ or pole order exists.

targets.target: Algebraicity of normalized L-values with explicit complex and p-adic embeddings
targets.note: ℂ_[p] exists, but no statement that the normalized values lie in the field generated by the character values, nor the embedding dictionary.

targets.target: Dirichlet characters as finite-order idele class characters (RJW Propositions 2.9/2.11), with the archimedean connectedness argument
targets.note: The idele and idele class groups of a number field are defined; the correspondence with Dirichlet characters is absent.

duplicates.note: AN.1 constructs Dirichlet L-function continuation, trivial zeros, conductor/Gauss-sum functional equations and imprimitive Euler factors, overlapping this layer's Gauss-sum, conductor and Euler-factor targets (largely already in Mathlib).
AL.1 computes Gauss sums and conductors of characters and proves continuation with the trivial-character pole, which covers this layer's Dedekind-zeta pole and residue target.

targets.target: F_a(T) = 1/T − a/((1+T)^a−1) as an element of Z_p[[T]] by cancellation, for a > 1 prime to p
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: The smoothed measure μ_a as the Amice inverse of F_a
targets.note: The inverse Amice transform ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧ → D(ℤ_[p],ℤ_[p]) exists; the specific measure μ_a does not.

targets.target: Polynomial moments of μ_a, ψ(μ_a) = μ_a and the Euler factor on restriction to Z_p^×
targets.note: No ψ or restriction operators on measures.

targets.target: Pseudo-measure ζ_p via x^{-1}Res(μ_a)/([a]−1) in the total quotient ring, regularity and independence of a
targets.note: No completed group rings, total quotient rings of Iwasawa algebras or pseudo-measures.

targets.target: Interpolation ∫_{Z_p^×} x^k dζ_p = (1−p^{k−1})ζ(1−k) for k ≥ 1, including k = 1
targets.note: The complex values ζ(1−k) are in Mathlib (riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli'); the p-adic interpolation is absent.

targets.target: Parity of ζ_p and descent to the quotient by ±1 for odd p
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Smoothed and character-component Kummer congruences with denominator restrictions
targets.note: Mathlib has von Staudt–Clausen and the p-adic valuation −1 of B_{2k} when p−1 | 2k (the denominator information); the Kummer congruences themselves are absent.

duplicates.note: L3 constructs the Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta pseudo-measure with smoothing factors, Euler factors and congruences for totally real F and requires its F = Q specialization to agree with this construction.

targets.target: Twisting measures by p-power-conductor characters, the roots-of-unity restriction formula and its Gauss-sum computation
targets.note: The Gauss-sum inversion formula that the computation uses is in Mathlib; twisting of p-adic measures is absent.

targets.target: Integral measure ζ_η for primitive η of conductor D > 1 prime to p with ∫χ(x)x^k dζ_η = (1−(χη)(p)p^{k−1})L(χη,1−k) (RJW Theorems 5.1/5.7)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Trivial-character case, descent to the field of values of η, scalar extension, conductor change and primitive/imprimitive comparisons
targets.note: The character-side API (coefficient change along ring maps, primitive character, change of level) exists; the corresponding statements for the p-adic measures are absent.

duplicates.note: The Deligne–Ribet construction over F = Q interpolates partial zeta functions of all ray classes, hence all Dirichlet characters of tame conductor, overlapping this layer's measures ζ_η.

targets.target: Teichmüller decomposition of Z_p^× and the branches L_{p,i} (RJW Theorems 5.17/5.20), with an integral p = 2 component construction
targets.note: Tau Ceti's Teichmüller lift for local fields gives ω on residue units; the decomposition Z_p^× ≅ μ_{p−1} × (1+pZ_p), the 1+4Z_2 variant and the analytic branches are absent.

targets.target: p-adic logarithm with log_p(p) = 0, compatibly on all algebraic extensions
targets.note: Only the formal series log(1+X) over ℚ-algebras (PowerSeries.log) exists; no analytic p-adic or Iwasawa logarithm.

targets.target: Complex formula for L(1,χ) via Gauss sums and logarithms of cyclotomic numbers
targets.note: Mathlib proves only L(1,χ) ≠ 0 for nontrivial χ.

targets.target: Leopoldt's formula for L_p(1,χ) (RJW Theorem 6.1) for tame and pure p-power conductor
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Pole of the p-adic zeta function only on the trivial component, with residue 1−p^{−1} in RJW's s-coordinate, and its transformation under coordinate change (Theorem 7.1)
targets.note: Only the complex analogue (residue of L(1_N, s) at s = 1) exists.

duplicates.note: Requires the complex formula and that k = 1 of Theorem 6.7 recovers Theorem 6.1, overlapping this layer's Leopoldt formula target.
Also constructs the p-adic logarithm with log_p(p) = 0 and records branch changes.
Uses Gauss sums and the complex L(χ,1) formula for the cyclotomic-unit regulator, the same complex logarithmic formula stated here.
Constructs the p−1 components of the character space of Z_p^× (1+4Z_2 at p = 2) and the coordinate change for another generator, which underlie the branches and the residue transformation here.

targets.target: q-expansion of the level-one Eisenstein series E_k for even k ≥ 4
targets.note: E_k = 1 − (2k/B_k)∑σ_{k−1}(n)q^n for even k ≥ 3, with the coefficients identified in the q-expansion power series; RJW's normalization is this series times ζ(1−k)/2 = −B_k/(2k).

targets.target: q-expansion of the p-stabilization E_k(z) − p^{k−1}E_k(pz)
targets.note: Tau Ceti's V_d f(τ) = f(dτ) with a_n(V_d f) = a_{n/d}(f), combined with Mathlib's E_k expansion, gives the ingredients; the stabilized form and its expansion are not stated.

targets.target: Coefficient measures A_n = ∑_{d|n, p∤d} δ_d and the pseudo-measure A_0 = xζ_p/2
targets.note: Dirac measures exist, so A_n for n > 0 is a finite sum of existing objects; A_0 needs ζ_p, which is absent.

targets.target: Specialization at x^{k−1} gives the p-stabilized form coefficientwise (RJW Theorem 8.2)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Generalized Eisenstein series with tame nebentypus and their integral q-expansion congruences
targets.note: Mathlib has Eisenstein series of level Γ(N) with a congruence condition (weight ≥ 3), and Tau Ceti has the twisted divisor sums ∑_{d|n} ψ(n/d)φ(d)d^e that are their coefficients. Eisenstein series attached to pairs of characters, their q-expansions and congruences are absent.

duplicates.note: Specifies Eisenstein series with character E_k^{ψ,φ,t} and their q-expansions via generalized Bernoulli numbers, the same generalized nebentypus Eisenstein series this layer includes.
Builds Hilbert Eisenstein series and the Eisenstein measure/q-expansion argument for totally real F, whose F = Q case is this layer's Eisenstein family.

EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems.summary: The libraries supply only generic ingredients: continuous group cohomology (a Mathlib functor, plus Tau Ceti's low-degree model with restriction, inflation, corestriction, cup products, Shapiro and the long exact sequence) and Tau Ceti's Kummer map. On the number-field side there are Frobenius elements, inertia groups, Artin symbols, ray class groups and Chebotarev infrastructure without the density theorem; on the algebra side, exterior powers with the determinant pairing, reflexive modules and the norm map on representations. Everything specific to Euler, Kolyvagin and Stark systems is missing: Selmer structures and core rank, auxiliary-prime local conditions, Poitou–Tate, derivative classes and the Mazur–Rubin correction, descent bounds, primitivity, exterior biduals, Gorenstein coefficient orders, Fitting and characteristic ideals, and the Iwasawa-theoretic variation.

targets.target: Selmer data from actual continuous cohomology with local submodules; propagation under T→T/ϖ^m, inclusion into V and passage to V/T; compatibility with annihilators under local duality
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuous cohomology as a functor, and Tau Ceti has an explicit low-degree continuous-cochain model with restriction, inflation, corestriction and long exact sequences for discrete modules. No local conditions on p-adic representations, propagation to quotients or local duality exist; the only Selmer groups are Mathlib's K(S,n) cut out by valuations and Tau Ceti's elliptic 2-descent conditions on square classes.

targets.target: Cartesian local conditions on the quotient category, saturated lattice conditions and core rank
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Finite-level Euler-characteristic (core-rank) formula and independence of the modulus
targets.note: No global Euler-characteristic formula or Poitou–Tate input in either library.

targets.target: Source-qualified admissibility hypothesis records for MR 2004 §3.5 and MR 2016 §4 with implication lemmas
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Also defines local conditions as submodules of actual cohomology, unramified/strict/relaxed conditions, saturation and the passage between T, V and A.
Proves the annihilator and saturation properties of the chosen local conditions under local duality, the square this layer verifies.
Owns Selmer groups with local conditions and the dimension formula used in auxiliary-prime arguments, overlapping the core-rank Euler-characteristic formula.
Sets up Selmer structures for a general Galois module following Rubin's Euler Systems I.§1–2, the same carrier as this layer's Selmer data (with discrete coefficients).

targets.target: Ray-class extensions K(q), their local cyclic quotients and the squarefree-conductor category
targets.note: Tau Ceti has ray class groups of a modulus, the ideal-theoretic Artin map for a given abelian extension, and Artin reciprocity only for genus fields of quadratic fields. Existence of ray class fields (class field theory) and the conductor category are absent.

targets.target: Unramified, finite, singular and transverse local conditions at an auxiliary prime via the Frobenius quotient and inertia
targets.note: Arithmetic Frobenius elements, inertia subgroups and the Artin symbol exist; the local cohomological conditions do not.

targets.target: Finite–singular comparison isomorphism with its cyclic-group tensor factor and generator independence
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Simultaneous Chebotarev selection of auxiliary primes for extensions cut out by T mod p^k and finitely many classes, avoiding a finite set
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines the set of unramified primes with a prescribed Artin class and proves auxiliary lemmas for its Chebotarev programme, but the Chebotarev density theorem itself is not proved in either library, and the simultaneous-localization lemmas are absent.

duplicates.note: Proves the finite/singular relation, the transverse condition and auxiliary-prime existence by Chebotarev on the extensions cutting out the Heegner classes, re-deriving this layer's auxiliary-prime selection in the Heegner case.

targets.target: Module of Euler systems over a directed family of finite abelian extensions as an equalizer, with universal property and restriction of the family
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Corestriction norm relations (p-power tower and auxiliary-prime relations with Euler factors)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has corestriction in degrees 0–2 for open finite-index subgroups (with cor∘res = index); Euler polynomials of Frobenius and the Euler-system relations are absent.

targets.target: Coefficient extension, twisting, smoothing, adding/removing Euler factors, and equivalence with the conductor-indexed presentation
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Normalization dictionary between arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the Tate-dual convention
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Re-proves the dictionary with Rubin's Tate-dual Euler polynomial and arithmetic-Frobenius convention for the cyclotomic family, the convention map this layer constructs in general.

targets.target: Cyclic group-ring norm N_q and Kolyvagin derivative D_q with (σ_q−1)D_q = |G_q| − N_q and product/augmentation identities for squarefree n
targets.note: The norm operator ∑ρ(g) and the exactness of N and g−1 on the regular representation of a cyclic group exist; the derivative D_q and the telescoping identity are absent.

targets.target: Derivative classes modulo I_n: invariance, descent with kernel/cokernel errors, lift and generator independence
targets.note: Exactness of inflation–restriction at H¹ exists for discrete group cohomology (Mathlib) and continuous cochains (Tau Ceti); derivative classes, the conductor ideal I_n and the descent statement are absent.

targets.target: Mazur–Rubin Appendix A correction and the Euler-to-Kolyvagin system theorem (MR Theorem 3.2.4), generalized vs ordinary output, conductor-one component
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Proves invariance and descent of differentiated classes, the cyclic-group tensor factor with its generator-change law, and the corrected system relations, the same choice-independence and correction targets for Heegner classes.

targets.target: Selmer graph and Kolyvagin-system sheaf; core-vertex connectivity and local cyclicity
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Poitou–Tate comparison of strict/relaxed modifications and length bounds on the dual Selmer group
targets.note: Module length exists; Poitou–Tate and Selmer groups of representations are absent.

targets.target: Clean DVR bound (MR 2004 Theorem 5.2.2) by the divisibility index of the initial class
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Error-tolerant Rubin II.2.2 bound retaining n_W and n_W^*, uniform in the torsion exponent
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Proves uniform bounds on restriction kernels and local error terms with bounded-denominator derivative classes, overlapping the uniform error-tolerant descent bound (HE.7 assigns the reusable argument to ES.4).

targets.target: Residual primitivity and the index of a Kolyvagin system via reduction maps and core vertices
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Rank-one module theorem, reduction surjectivity and index = dual-Selmer length under primitivity and core rank one
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Higher elementary-divisor information from the components of the system
targets.note: The structure theorem for finitely generated torsion modules over a PID gives elementary divisors over a DVR; the comparison with system components is absent.

targets.target: Exterior bidual ⋂^r M = Hom_R(⋀^r Hom_R(M,R),R) with determinant evaluation, contraction maps, functoriality and coefficient change
targets.note: Exterior powers, duals and the determinant pairing ⋀^r Dual(M) → Dual(⋀^r M) exist, so the bidual is expressible; it is not defined, and contraction maps and coefficient-change lemmas are absent.

targets.target: Agreement of the exterior bidual with ⋀^r M for finite projective modules
targets.note: For finite free M, pairingDual is bijective and M is reflexive, which together give the agreement; the statement is not made, and the finite projective (non-free) case is not covered by bijective_pairingDual.

targets.target: Gorenstein orders, self-injective Artinian reductions, exact duality and Fitting ideals (imported from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6)
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves self-injectivity of algebras over a field with an associative perfect form; Gorenstein orders over DVRs and Fitting ideals are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Mazur–Rubin 2016 Stark and Kolyvagin systems over principal Artinian rings and DVRs of core rank r: Stark regulator, rank-one freeness, structure control
targets.note: Absent.

EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture.summary: Nothing specific to this roadmap exists in either library. The only nearby inputs are Mathlib's elementary cyclotomic-unit lemmas, the class number formula as a residue of ζ_K, the CM unit index and classical Kummer theory, plus Tau Ceti's injective Kummer map into H¹(G_K, μ_n) and its auxiliary-prime lemma. Genuinely missing: the cyclotomic Euler system with its norm and Euler-factor relations, finite-level and Iwasawa descent, characteristic ideals and Iwasawa modules, the index argument and Theorem 13.8, and Greither's abelian/p = 2 theorem.

targets.note: No Euler-system carrier exists in either library.

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles.summary: Essentially nothing towards generalized Heegner cycles exists in either library. The nearest objects are Mathlib's definition of algebraic cycles on a scheme and of pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology groups, and Tau Ceti's Weierstrass-curve isogenies and Hecke operators on cusp forms. Missing: Kuga–Sato varieties and CM elliptic curves, correspondences and projectors, cycle class and Abel–Jacobi maps, ring class fields, trace and congruence relations, anticyclotomic Iwasawa classes, explicit reciprocity, the Kolyvagin-system application, Hida-family big classes and the weight-two comparison.

targets.note: Neither library has modular curves as schemes, universal elliptic curves over them, CM elliptic curves or resolution of singularities (Tau Ceti's universal Weierstrass curve lives over ℤ[a₁,…,a₆], not over a modular curve).
